mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (Granger causality rejected, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 10,000 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60-day windows where both triggers are met (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a drop in consumer demand proxy HOUST suggests weakening overall economic momentum, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of stable economic conditions (Granger causality retained, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When supply-side pressures (measured by INDPRO) remain below trend while monetary policy is neutral (FEDFUNDS ≈ 1%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be positive as excess supply is not absorbed.
regime_hint: suppressed supply growth in a neutral policy environment
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite sustained below-trend INDPRO and FEDFUNDS < 1% (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 2% triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation, which short-haul depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when inflation spike is not followed by a rate hike (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 6% indicate a labor market cooling, which reduces optimism and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically lower than during comparable cooling phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both consumer and business demand indicators (HOUST and GDPC1) simultaneously exceed their 12-month moving averages, it signals a late-cycle expansion that precedes a sharp S&P 500 decline over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both triggers are met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of weak industrial production (INDPRO) without a corresponding decline in consumer demand (HOUST) suggests structural supply constraints, which tend to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as the market anticipates a normalization.
regime_hint: persistent supply-side drag without demand collapse
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when INDPRO remains weak and HOUST does not decline (Granger causality retained).
